reviewer_challenge: Same host and log does not show the same actor. Record IDs interleave in time, but C has no network link to 10.0.2.19.
evidence_in_logs: Logon IDs: A=0x3e7 (SYSTEM), B=0x1d313d (IEUser), C=0xffe4 (IEUser processes) and 0x3e7 (SYSTEM service VSSVC); the two IEUser sessions differ, and 0x3e7 is the shared SYSTEM session, which does not identify an actor; 11 and 315 record IDs missing between files.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: A network or logon event in C tying it to 10.0.2.19 (absent).
outcome: Upheld: actor claim stays Low; host/log claim stays Medium.

reviewer_challenge: Remote origin rests on a 335 ms gap between T01 (inbound SMB) and T03 (service registry write). No shared session ID links them.
evidence_in_logs: T02 shows the \ntsvcs pipe opened by System; file A contains no sc.exe process record, which argues against a local sc create. But the files are excerpts, so absence is weak.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: Security 4624/7045 events or a full Sysmon log showing no sc.exe.
outcome: Partly upheld: service creation stays High; remote SMB origin lowered to Medium.

reviewer_challenge: A single outbound TCP connection is not proof of a reverse shell or C2. No traffic content or repeated beaconing is logged.
evidence_in_logs: T09 shows pid 2484 connecting to 10.0.2.19:4444; the pid matches T07. Nothing shows data exchanged.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: Packet capture or a second connection event showing sustained traffic.

reviewer_challenge: Source image in T08 is truncated ("50\Windows\..."), so the record may be unreliable as evidence of injection.
evidence_in_logs: T08 SourceProcessGUID equals the ProcessGuid of T06 (pid 3872) and TargetProcessGUID equals that of T07 (pid 2484). T07 names 3872 as its parent. CallTrace passes through managed .NET modules (mscorwks, System.ni), consistent with PowerShell starting a child.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: A Sysmon event 8 or 25 (remote thread / process tampering) against pid 2484.
outcome: Answered: GUIDs resolve the truncated path; parent-handle explanation strengthened; stays Low.

reviewer_challenge: Start=4 shows a value change only. "Clean-up" assigns intent the log cannot show.
evidence_in_logs: T10 is one registry write 1.2 s after T03; no key-deletion event.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: Registry key deletion or service-removal event.
outcome: Upheld: reworded as an observation (service disabled); intent unknown.

reviewer_challenge: "Impacket" is inferred from a file-name pattern (__<epoch>) and cmd.exe /Q /c redirection to ADMIN$. Other tools reimplement this pattern.
evidence_in_logs: Pattern matches wmiexec-style tools; the epoch 1556656369 = 20:32:49 UTC matches T11.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: Tool artefacts on the sender, or Security logon events.

reviewer_challenge: "Interactive shell" is unproven. A script or handler can send a command to a waiting cmd.exe without a human.
evidence_in_logs: T25 parent pid 2892 equals T24 pid 2892; the gap is 3 min 18 s.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: Keystroke timing, or other commands at irregular intervals.
outcome: Upheld: reworded to "command shell that later ran whoami".

reviewer_challenge: Timeline order differs from record order at T09 and T10 (record 9813 has an earlier event time than record 9812). Which order is authoritative?
evidence_in_logs: Sysmon UtcTime is stamped when the event occurs; the record is written later (network events lag by about 1.3 s).
evidence_that_would_distinguish: Sysmon documentation on UtcTime versus record write time.
outcome: Answered: event-time order kept; method documented on the method slide.

reviewer_challenge: Sysmon event 2 records any creation-time change and does not show intent. Both events set the same value, which is what copying a package while keeping its original creation time would produce.
evidence_in_logs: T18 (Temp\302a23.msi) and T20 (C:\Windows\Installer\304d1c.msi) both set CreationUtcTime to 22:43:38.892, 5 min 20 s before T18. T18 and T20 are the only event-2 records among the 25 events. Checked against timeline.csv; raw EVTX not re-read.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: The source package's own creation time, or $MFT $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME times (neither is in these logs).
outcome: Upheld: stays Low; timestomping unsupported (v2 wording already narrow).

reviewer_challenge: Starting VSSVC.exe shows the Volume Shadow Copy service started. It does not show a shadow copy was created, changed or deleted, and no shadow-copy command appears in the 25 events.
evidence_in_logs: T19: services.exe starts VSSVC.exe 0.25 s after T18 (msiexec event). No vssadmin, wmic or diskshadow process creation in any of the 25 events (searched timeline.csv). The files are excerpts, so absence is weak.
evidence_that_would_distinguish: VSS or System log events, vssadmin list shadows before and after, or a deletion command in a full Sysmon log.
outcome: Upheld: stays Rejected; VSSVC start shows no tampering.
